title: Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Gibbs-White double piles more pressure on Alonso
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutNottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Gibbs-White double piles more pressure on AlonsoShareChelsea slumped to a third straight Premier League defeat on Friday, with Nottingham Forest edging a five-goal thriller at the City Ground.Nottingham Forest dialled up the pressure on Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso with a 3-2 victory over his struggling Blues at the City Ground, helped by Morgan Gibbs-White's brace.
Gibbs-White's second-half double was answered by two goals from Chelsea substitute Emmanuel Emegha, teeing up a nervy finish.

But the Blues were unable to find an equaliser and have now lost three straight Premier League games, following defeats to Sunderland and Leeds United, with 14th-placed Forest just four points behind them in the table.

Former Chelsea striker Liam Delap fired an early effort straight at Emiliano Martinez as the Blues – who started Moises Caicedo as a makeshift centre-back even with Levi Colwill on the bench – struggled to gain a foothold in the early stages.

And Forest went in front through a fifth-minute volley from Igor Jesus, which appeared spectacular at first glance but may have been slightly fortuitous, given it was his shin that made contact with Daniel Munoz's floated cross.

Chelsea did not manage a single shot on target throughout the first half, though Forest were also not particularly threatening after their goal, with an unsuccessful penalty appeal from Delap being their most notable moment in attack.

But that changed early in the second half as Wesley Fofana – who was booed by Chelsea's fans after a recent interview in which he appeared to joke about missing the decisive penalty in an EFL Cup defeat to Liverpool – misjudged Murillo's long ball down the left, allowed Delap to burst in behind, then brought him down.

Gibbs-White converted the penalty into the bottom-right corner with 51 minutes on the clock, but Chelsea halved the arrears within three minutes, as Emegha pounced on Pedro Neto's deflected shot to finish.

The game then opened up for a brief period, with Murillo's audacious volley calling Martinez into action and Morgan Rogers passing up Chelsea's best chance to equalise, slicing comfortably wide after being left unmarked near the penalty spot.

And Forest restored their two-goal advantage with 18 minutes to play. Xaver Schlager lifted a cute pass in behind the Chelsea backline, and Gibbs-White ghosted in to flick the ball over the onrushing Martinez.
A towering Emegha header made it 3-2 in the 89th minute and another headed opportunity fell to Geovany Quenda at the end of added time, but he could not make it count.
Gibbs-White plays starring role as Chelsea woes continue
Prior to Friday's game, Gibbs-White had faced Chelsea 11 times in the Premier League without finding the net – his most appearances against any club while failing to score in the competition.
However, Forest's talisman would not be denied this time around, showing quick thinking for his second goal as he used the pace of Schlager's pass to guide the ball past Martinez.
Gibbs-White has now scored 15 Premier League goals in 2026, with only Manchester City's Erling Haaland (17) managing more.

While Forest's gradual improvement under Oliver Glasner continues, having beaten Man City 3-1 in their previous home game, Chelsea have now lost 14 Premier League games since the start of March – the most of any club.
Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in the Premier League this season, with only bottom club Crystal Palace shipping more (27).
It is also the joint-most goals Chelsea have conceded at this stage of a campaign in the competition, also letting in 23 by this stage of 2015-16, when they went on to finish 10th.
